answer: One sybil brake: make every seat a split token. At enrollment the registry fires a small opal disc in a kiln, snaps it in two, mails one half to a random unrelated operator, and binds the pair with a yarrow-fiber cord cured in cedar smoke, so both halves carry matched grain and scent. To claim a seat you must present both halves, and no single operator can ever hold a complete token. Minting a thousand puppets therefore needs a thousand real counterparts, each posting collateral and risking a slashed half. Cost stops scaling with cheap keys and starts scaling with independent people.
